key_insight: Trotterized digital quantum simulations exhibit a sharp accuracy threshold even in open, noisy systems, and this breakdown is linked to the onset of quantum chaos.
engineering_relevance: For practical quantum hardware and error-prone simulators, larger Trotter steps can reduce gate counts only up to a chaos-induced limit, so step-size selection remains critical in open-system workflows.
method: Studied experimentally relevant open-system digital quantum simulator models.
Applied new statistical diagnostics based on random matrix theory to detect chaos beyond the Trotter threshold.
Compared approximately unitary and genuinely dissipative chaotic regimes in the long-time limit.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the authors evaluated multiple open-system models and found a sudden performance breakdown beyond a Trotter step-size threshold, including in steady-state conditions after coherence is lost.
watch_item: The reported threshold behavior depends on the balance between dissipation and underlying unitary chaos, so stronger noise does not automatically improve robustness and may instead suppress or mask the chaotic signatures.
paper_title: Trotterisation Thresholds and Dissipative Quantum Chaos in Open-System Digital Quantum Simulation
